After the shot I had flu like symptoms and stayed in bed for 48 hours. The first day I didn't take any medication, but I did take medication on the second day. I slept through it the first day. Then around 11/15/2022, I started getting sick with what seemed like an upper respiratory infection. Then it turned into chest congestion with head congestion. Then it turned into a sinus infection and all these symptoms occurred at the same time. I never had a fever. I tested twice for COVID-19 and both were negative. During this time, I had also taken 2 weeks worth of MUCINEX to try and combat this before calling the doctor. When I went to see my doctor, I went to get a chest x-ray and I realized I needed something to combat this. I was given a steroid, 8 day course of prednisone. I was also given doxycycline for 20 days. I felt well for exactly 2 days, 48 hours. That was around 01/01 and 01/02 where I felt well. I had no chest congestion, no wheezing, no post nasal drip. Around 01/03/2023, the symptoms started again and it's progressively getting worse up to today. Today, I have wheezing, coughing, a possible sinus infection/congestion and post nasal drip. I'm coughing so bad that it's in the upper bronchial tract. There's thick mucus that has been choking me. When I wheeze bad, I start coughing really badly and I can only force something to come up a couple times a day. According to my tests, no COVID-19 and no fever.

I was very sick following the third vaccine and it started a course of me being out of work for 9 months on disability as I saw an array of specialists searching for help. I had adverse effects to the first two vaccines but my symptoms became far worse after the third one. I did not know what was wrong with me at the time but felt like I was having a heart attack and made several trips to doctors offices complaining of tachycardia, faitness, shortness of breath and adrenaline rushes. With time my symptoms became worse and not better. I evenutally collapsed in the classroom on January 25th 2022 leading to illness so severe I was barely able to get out of bed. My husband became my care provider and I was unable to work. I was diagnosed with POTS, as well as Small Fiber Neuropathy. Neither of which I had prior to the third vaccine. I also started having sever blood sugar issues and was diagnosed with hypoglycemia. I now have to wear a continuous glucose monitor, I am taking beta blockers and I have a nurse come to my home once a week to administer an IV. I have a very restrictive diet as my body can no longer tolerate carbohydrates or sugar.

narrative: On 03/07 I saw my PCP because of the two incidents of being awoken with pain in my left rib cage and extreme shortness of breath. In addition, I had a lot of burping so I was thinking it was gastrointestinal discomfort. She ruled that out and thought I was having a pulmonary embolism and said to go to the ER. I went to the ER and I had a CT scan and it was determined that I had blood clots in both lungs. I had a Heparin drip for 24 hours and they kept me over night. They sent me home with Eliquis starter back 10 mg twice daily for a week, then 5 mgs twice daily for the rest of the 30 days. My PCP prescribed it for 90 days with a recommended follow up CT scan in 3 months. In the hospital, they did an ultrasound for my legs and there were no DVTs. They also did an echocardiogram and there was nothing there to indicate any connection. The cause of the blood clots is unknown. I did not have any lengthy plane rides, road trips, surgeries, etc. that could have caused this. As recommended by the hospital, I did have follow ups with my PCP, cardiologist and pulmonologist. I don't have the pain or shortness of breath anymore. I do have shortness of breath occasionally, but I did have shortness of breath on exertion prior to this event. I have no idea if this is in relation to the vaccine.

narrative: fainted; sweating/Diaphoresis; have pain in the lower back of the head and back of his neck; have pain in the lower back of the head and back of his neck; generalized weakness; dizziness; shaking; blood pressure was a little low at 91/51; This is a spontaneous report received from a contactable reporter(s) (Physician) from medical information team.  A 16-year-old male patient received meningococcal group b Rlp2086 (TRUMENBA), on 04Apr2022 as dose 1, single (Batch/Lot number: unknown) for immunisation; meningococcal vaccine a/c/y/w conj (dip tox) (MENACTRA), on 04Apr2022 as dose number unknown, single (Batch/Lot number: unknown) for immunisation. The patient's relevant medical history and concomitant medications were not reported. The following information was reported: DIZZINESS (hospitalization) with onset 04Apr2022, outcome "recovering"; ASTHENIA (hospitalization) with onset 04Apr2022, outcome "recovering", described as "generalized weakness"; HEADACHE (hospitalization), NECK PAIN (hospitalization) all with onset 04Apr2022, outcome "recovering" and all described as "have pain in the lower back of the head and back of his neck"; TREMOR (hospitalization) with onset 04Apr2022, outcome "recovering", described as "shaking"; HYPERHIDROSIS (hospitalization) with onset 04Apr2022, outcome "recovering", described as "sweating/Diaphoresis"; SYNCOPE (hospitalization, medically significant), outcome "recovering", described as "fainted"; HYPOTENSION (medically significant), outcome "recovering", described as "blood pressure was a little low at 91/51". The events "sweating/diaphoresis", "have pain in the lower back of the head and back of his neck", "generalized weakness", "dizziness" and "shaking" required emergency room visit. Therapeutic measures were taken as a result of syncope, hyperhidrosis, headache, neck pain, asthenia, dizziness, tremor, hypotension. Clinical course: The patient received his first dose of Trumenba, as well as Menactra on 04Apr2022. Trumenba and Menactra are routinely given together. He had a well visit at 1pm and did not immediately have any issues and was fine when he left the office. His mother reported he had nothing to eat or drink prior to his 1pm appointment. Forty-five minutes later he went to withheld with a parent and he began to have pain in the lower back of the head and back of his neck, generalized weakness, dizziness, shaking, and sweating/diaphoresis. They called 911 and he had to go to the ER. There his blood pressure was a little low at 91/51. He was given two liters of normal saline and the IV medications administered were benadryl, toradol and reglan. He had a CT scan of the brain which came back normal. Then when he was getting up to leave he again got weak, experienced dizziness, and sweating and then fainted. He was admitted overnight for IV fluids. While admitted he had a cardiology and neurology consult. Overnight he continued to improve, he had a heart echo done, he had no symptoms and was discharged the next day.  The information on the batch/lot number for meningococcal group b Rlp2086 has been requested and will be submitted if and when received.; Sender's Comments: There is a reasonable possibility that the event syncope and headache were related to TRUMENBA use based on known drug safety profile. Based on the close temporal relationship, the association between the events hyperhidrosis, neck pain, asthenia, dizziness, and tremor with TRUMENBA can not be fully excluded. The association between the event hypotension with TRUMENBA can not be fully excluded.  The impact of this report on the benefit/risk profile of the Pfizer product is evaluated as part of Pfizer procedures for safety evaluation, including the review and analysis of aggregate data for adverse events. Any safety concern identified as part of this review, as well as any appropriate action in response, will be promptly notified to regulatory authorities, Ethics Committees, and Investigators, as appropriate.

narrative: I thought I had allergy symptoms at first.  My husband and I had a little sneezing, runny nose, never stuffy.  I don't think I ever ran a temperature.  That evening I finally got a hold of my doctor.  They did a Telehealth with my doctor office.  I couldn't say two or three words without coughing. I was able to start Paxlovid medicine immediately.  The next day I was feeling much better.  The day after that I didn't know I was sick.  By the fourth day I was fine.

I had my vaccination on 10/05/2022. I was driving on 01/16/2023 and I started to experience severe dizziness and I wanted to pass out. I pulled my car over and hoped someone would find me. A volunteer paramedic found me in the parking lot and called 911. I was very scared when it happened but I did not hurt. I had a MRI and CAT scan done at the emergency room. I was told I had cerebellar stroke syndrome. I am given different medication to make the plaque slimy in my body so it will help me if this happens again. I am being followed up with neurology and medical team.
